items.title: Compare a verse, with Plus
items.note: Looked at 2026-11-07, not built, for his word on one thing. Compare shows a verse in each Bible the app may show, and the downloaded ones keep their own numbering (BIBLES.md): the Synodal counts a psalm's title as its first verses (its Psalm 50:3 is the app's 50:1) and follows the Hebrew order in Jeremiah, the Greek divides Joel in four chapters. So each downloaded Bible needs its verses placed against the app's first, which is also what notes, highlights and the Fathers need in those Bibles. The cleanest source for that is the Copenhagen Alliance's versification mappings (the United Bible Societies, SIL, Tyndale House and YouVersion; github.com/Copenhagen-Alliance/versification-specification), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0: a map made from it would have to be credited and shared under the same licence. His word: use it, or have the maps made from the texts themselves, as the KJV to Septuagint map was (slower, and what cannot be placed stays out).

items.title: The app's Psalms 113, 114 and 115 are divided as the Hebrew divides them, not as the Septuagint the Church prays: an Orthodox reader's Psalm 115 ("I believed, wherefore I have spoken") is the app's 115:10
items.note: Found by the verse map. The app's data has 113 at 8 verses, 114 at 18, 115 at 19 (the Hebrew 114, 115 and 116 whole); Brenton's edition and the Septuagint have 113 at 26 (Hebrew 114 and 115), 114 at 9 and 115 at 10 (Hebrew 116 in two). The line under each title, from lib/bible/psalmNumbers.ts, describes the Septuagint's division, so on these three pages it names the wrong Hebrew psalm, and a search for Psalm 116 opens the app's 114. The fix is to divide the three as Brenton does; it moves any note or highlight a reader put on them, so it waits for his word. The cross-references are right either way: the map follows the words

items.title: Candlelight at Vespers
items.note: Built 2026-11-07. One switch, Candlelight at Vespers, under the palettes in the reader's settings and in Settings, Reading: while it is on, the app reads in Candlelight from sunset to sunrise and in the reader's own palette by day. Sunset is reckoned for the city of the phone's time zone (data/calendar/zone-coords.json, 542 zones from the tz database, public domain, made by scripts/zone-coords.mjs), never from its location: no permission, nothing about where a reader is leaves the phone. The sums are the almanac's (lib/calendar/sun.ts), held within a few minutes of the known times for London, Los Angeles, Sydney and Bucharest; where the sun does not set, six to six. The night is kept on the device so the app opens after dark already in Candlelight (lib/reader/prepaint.ts), and the theme controller turns it at sunset and sunrise and on waking. Plus, as Candlelight is. Walked in a browser in Bucharest's zone on 7 November: on at 20:00, Candlelight from the first paint at 21:30, the reader's Light at noon the next day. The chips still light the reader's own palette at night, which is theirs

items.title: Decide the red commentary dots (flag 5)
Keep the coming week's daily readings on the phone by themselves, on Wi-Fi, for Plus
items.note: Built 2026-11-07, on Android (lib/readAloud/week.ts). When the app opens and comes back to the front, for a reader with a sure yes to Plus, on Wi-Fi only (never mobile data, never a connection the phone cannot name): every chapter read aloud that the Church reads in the next seven days by the reader's calendar is saved as a saved book is, and noted as the week's; once its last day has passed the week takes it away, unless the reader saved its book themselves. The reader's own saving goes first. On by default for Plus, as "by themselves" asks; Settings, On this device, has the switch and what it keeps (off takes it all away). A week on the new calendar is 15 to 17 chapters (counted for four weeks from 7 November 2026 to Holy Week 2027); the old calendar's days carry fewer readings in the app, so fewer. Not on iPhone yet: the recordings are kept in the folder iCloud backs up, and a week's worth every week on its own would make that worse (c-ios-offline-backup, waiting for his word). Tests: lib/readAloud/__tests__/week.test.ts. Walked in a browser as the app: the switch and its count; not walked on a phone Read over the same evening, and one race mended: a reader who tapped Save on a book while the week was fetching a chapter of it would have had that chapter marked the week's, and taken out of their saved book once its day had passed. A book the reader saves is now recorded as theirs until they take it off the phone, and the week marks none of its chapters (lib/readAloud/weekKept.ts; the race held by lib/readAloud/__tests__/week.test.ts, which fails without the guard).

items.title: Check
items.note: Checked 2026-11-07, and the answer to both was no: the saving lived in the screen's memory, so a signal lost half way failed every chapter after it, closing the app ended it, Save again fetched the whole book again, and it saved over mobile data without asking. Built the same day: the book being saved is kept on the device until every chapter is (lib/readAloud/saving.ts); chapters already saved are skipped, so it goes on from where it stopped; on mobile data it waits for Wi-Fi, with Use mobile data and Cancel on the line over the player's controls; with no signal it waits for one; it goes on by itself when the connection allows, the next time the app opens included (components/native/SavingBridge.tsx); a move from Wi-Fi to mobile data stops it after the chapter in hand. Through @capacitor/network, already in both apps' builds and now used for the first time. Tests: lib/readAloud/__tests__/saving.test.ts. Walked in a browser as the app: waiting for Wi-Fi, Cancel, waiting for a signal, then all 21 chapters of John saved by themselves when Wi-Fi came. Not walked on a phone: the plugin's native answers (wifi, cellular) are its own. Waiting for Wi-Fi is the default on mobile data, as the big listening apps do; his word can make it save at once instead

Measured again on 3630ea0b (after the dock, the plans page, the Nativity plan, the Florilegium starters, the timeline pictures and the Thread): 239.3 MB on disk, 75.1 MB packed; 0.7 MB of room left. The full optimize, his "do everything you can that's safe" of 2026-11-07: the loading placeholders written short, the Greek packed, the shop's photos streamed. Measured on d2c711b2: 217.7 MB on disk, 69.5 MB packed (from 239.3 and 75.1): 22.3 MB of room on disk, 15.5 MB packed. Not done, and why: Next's own payload overhead (37 MB, its format), the commentary repeating the works (0.4 MB), fonts, ambience and icons (needed offline). items.title: On an iPhone, offline listening keeps its recordings in the iCloud-backed Documents folder, which Apple's storage rules keep for what cannot be downloaded again
items.note: Found while choosing where the downloaded Bibles go: the Filesystem plugin's Data is Documents on iOS. The Bibles use LibraryNoCloud (kept, not backed up; Android's own files, as before). lib/readAloud/offline.ts saves recordings with Data, a review risk and up to hours of audio in the reader's iCloud. items.title: Community's page for a new post: the first words no longer folded its head
items.note: Found 2026-11-07 by the export walk (section 47, at 390 and 360 wide). The page folds its head on the first words by scrolling until the doors are under the bar (components/community/ComposePage.tsx, from 1.8 build 87); the scroll was asked for, and ended the same moment by the caret of the letter typed: Chrome 153, the engine of the Android WebView, ends a smooth scroll when a field inside it reveals its caret, and a field does so on every letter. Older than 1.9; nothing in the page changed since 1 November. Fixed the same day: the scroll goes a frame at a time (lib/ui/glideScroll.ts, at once when the reader asked for less motion, stopped by a finger), which a caret cannot end; held by lib/ui/__tests__/glideScroll.test.ts and walked in the rebuilt export. A phone was not walked.

items.title: The export walk caught up with 1.9's designs, and says once when an export was built with the shop off
items.note: The first whole walk of the 1.9 export (2026-11-07): 1391 checks passed, 28 did not, and only two of the 28 were the app: Community's new post did not fold its head (c-compose-fold, older than 1.9). Seventeen were checks still looking for screens his 1.9 picks replaced: the verse's pill (now the verse strip, his pick B; 3 checks), the plans as a list (now Continue, the season's card and picture tiles, his pick for Practice; 1 check, and 12 more in section 40 that followed from its first tap) and Settings ending in data and Purify (now data, what this device keeps, and Purify; 1). Nine were one missing flag: the export had been built without NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOP_ENABLED, which both release workflows set, so every page of the shop was a 404 while still in the bundle, and section 10's own test for a shop left out passed it by. scripts/export-walk.mjs now reads the strip, the tiles and the storage group, and says first, once, when the shop was built off, with the flags to set. On an export built as the releases build it, the nine sections that had failed walk 244 of 244. Then the whole walk on that export (the code of 0ec04070, before the lock counts and the week's race fix): 1488 of 1488, more than before because sections 40 and 47 now run to their end.

items.title: Count which lock a reader taps, and which leads to a purchase
items.note: From the Plus brainstorm of 2026-11-06 (BRAINSTORM.md, "What nobody can see"), item 12 of PLAN.md. Built 2026-11-07: the upgrade sheet (components/billing/UpgradeModal.tsx) counts lock_tapped with the feature it opens on, and plus_bought when a purchase in it goes through, with the feature and the plan; each with the kind of device, kept to the day, no session, account, device id or page (lib/analytics/lockCounting.ts and lockCount.ts; the server's closed list in lib/security/schemas.ts). No migration: analytics_events takes any name. The admin reads it at Money, Subscriptions, Locks (7, 30 or 90 days: met, bought, the rate, a year or a month, by feature). Not counted: purchases on the pricing page, and restores. On the iPhone nothing is locked until the App Store sells Plus, so iPhone readers meet no lock. For his word before the release: the privacy page's paragraph saying so (drafted in app/(app)/privacy/page.tsx), and the 1.9 letter must list the change, as the page's own "Changes to this page" promises. Held by lib/analytics/__tests__/lockCounting.test.ts; the admin panel is drawn there, not walked (the admin needs a signed-in admin).
